itens.t: SpaceX Fires Up Starship Upper Stage Ahead of Landmark Flight 15 Test Launch

itens.d:
Astronomers using the Vera Rubin Observatory have discovered a mysterious dwarf planet candidate orbiting beyond Neptune. Designated 2026 ED138, the icy object measures between 600 and 1,500 kilometers wide, making it large enough for gravity to shape it into a sphere.

The object was found on October 13 by Matthew Holman using search code developed with Kevin Napier at the Center for Astrophysics. If confirmed, it would join a very small group of recognized dwarf planets in our solar system, which currently includes Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake.
